reasons: The current product fit is partial or carries unresolved scope limits.
allowed_claims: The API is available on all plans, including the free plan
Buttondown's API is rate-limited to prevent abuse, with limits described as generous enough for most use cases
Buttondown will migrate a user's mailing list to Buttondown for free, regardless of list size, via a concierge migration service
Buttondown does not charge extra for paid subscribers on its paid subscriptions feature, letting creators keep all revenue they make
Buttondown is GDPR-compliant and does not collect any data about users or their subscribers by default
Buttondown takes no cut of newsletter sponsorships; creators keep 100% of every sponsorship minus Stripe's processing fee
Buttondown supports over 40 integrations for embedding videos, GIFs, songs, posts, or other content
Buttondown lets users send a newsletter post directly from their personal or business email by emailing it in, and save it as a draft by sending to a different address
Buttondown charges users based on total subscriber count across all their newsletters, not by the number of newsletters created, so users can create unlimited distinct newsletters
Buttondown for Teams lets collaborators review emails before they go out, seeing drafts, suggesting changes, and helping ship with confidence
Teams access control lets you give an editor access to drafts but not billing, and let a marketing lead manage subscribers without touching API keys
Buttondown is free for the first 100 subscribers
The Teams add-on costs an additional $79/month
The Email attachments add-on costs an additional $9/month
Registered 501(c)(3) non-profits (or the equivalent in their country) get a 50% discount on their plan
Buttondown charges for active subscribers only, not all contacts
Buttondown's listed prices assume sending at most one email a day to the entire subscriber base; sending more requires contacting them about usage-based pricing
Buttondown webhooks let an external application react to events, with the documentation's own example being pointing a webhook at Slack to create a notification.
Exceeding the daily subscriber-creation cap does not return a standard rate-limit 429; instead it returns a 400 that points the caller to the imports endpoint as the supported bulk-onboarding path.
Buttondown's public API documents a POST /v1/emails endpoint that creates an email, and the sample request shows it can be created with a status implying it is sent/scheduled from code.
Creating an email via the API instantly triggers sending, based on tags and email type provided — confirming the emails endpoint composes and sends newsletter emails programmatically.
The API supports scheduling a newsletter send by setting status and publish_date on a POST to /v1/emails.
A draft email can be sent out by updating its status to 'about_to_send', at which point Buttondown automatically begins sending it.

POST /v1/subscribers is rate limited to one hundred requests per day by default, growing over time, with a contact path for higher limits, and import via CSV is suggested specifically for initial bulk import rather than ongoing volume.
unresolved_objections: Does Buttondown publish runnable example scripts or a hosted trigger mechanism that would let an operator automate sends without running their own server?
